# Note-mark line metrics

Original XML generated by `tools/note_mark_metrics_fixture.py`; no font binaries
or third-party document assets are included. The reference application exported `native.pdf`
without saving the source. `tools/record_note_mark_metrics.py` records source/PDF
hashes and native text positions in `reference.json`.

43 cases compare literal digits, footnoteRef and endnoteRef with two fonts,
baseline/superscript/subscript, positive/negative explicit position, default,
single, expanded and compressed automatic line spacing, note-only paragraphs,
and larger paragraph-mark formatting. These are orphan marks, not actual notes.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.11.6 and 17.11.13 permit ignoring orphan marks; the reference
application displays them. Section 17.3.1.33 describes automatic line spacing but does not specify this
mark-specific calculation. The reference application includes note marks in natural line allocation
while excluding them from the text metrics used for the line-spacing multiplier.
In note-only paragraphs the paragraph mark supplies the spacing metrics and a
minimum total height; ordinary text otherwise determines spacing. The note's
descent is preserved when the paragraph-mark minimum raises the baseline.

Browser checks compare native baselines of ordinary text and following lines.
They intentionally do not claim that font-dependent script glyph sizing matches;
that remains an independent issue. Explicit-position cases retain an existing
sub-half-point rounding difference and use a 0.6pt bound; all others use 0.25pt.
